name: Cathedral-Of-Static

civilization.name: The Cantorate
civilization.notes: Desert-dwelling culture that treated radio noise as scripture; their final transmissions were made inside the monolith field, and no record explains what they heard there.

specific_features: Monolithic structures of unknown origin standing in ranks across the dust, all aligned toward one distant point
Signal of unknown origin broadcasting layered static that resolves, briefly, into voices speaking dead languages
Radiation hotspot burning at the precise point where the monolith alignments converge
description: A world of rust-colored dust and shattered glass, where the horizon bends around dunes the size of mountain ranges. Days burn amber through a thin amber sky; nights fall fast and hard, dropping forty degrees in an hour. Out of the dust seas rise the monoliths—several thousand basalt slabs, each taller than a spire, ranked in formation like a congregation awaiting a sermon.

Walking among them is disquieting in ways visitors struggle to name. The silence is total, yet every suit radio carries a faint wash of static that grows louder nearer the alignment's focal point. Old-timer prospectors swear the static changes pitch at dusk. Nothing else moves except the wind, and the wind does not enter the monolith rows.

The Cantorate flourished here for nine centuries and left behind temples tuned like antennas, hymnals written in interference patterns, and mass graves oriented toward the same converging point as the stones. Their last recorded transmission was made from that point and consists of sixty-one hours of static. Then their cities emptied, their reactors ran down, and no skeleton has ever been found.

Every survey drone sent to the convergence point has failed at the same coordinates, and every crewed expedition has turned back short of it—headaches, instrument drift, dreams reported across comms that no one remembers making. The uranium is real and the claim stakes are cheap. The question no company will print in its brochures is whether the static is a recording, or a listening.
